title: Shooting and footage
description: The words of filming: what a camera records, how a shot is framed and what you call the pieces you bring into an editor.
intro: These are the words people use before editing starts: the camera, the shot and the raw video you bring in.

title: Editing and timeline
description: The words of the editing screen: project, timeline, tracks, clips, playhead, markers, undo and the other tools you use every day.
intro: These are the parts of the editing screen and the things you do there every day.

title: Cuts and transitions
description: How one shot leads to the next: kinds of cuts, fades, dissolves, wipes and the edits that move the cut point.
intro: A video is a chain of shots. These words describe how one shot turns into the next.

title: Audio
description: Sound in video: volume, decibels, loudness, fades, ducking, music beats and the words a sound editor uses.
intro: Half of a video is what you hear. These are the words for sound.

title: Color
description: How video stores and shows colour: brightness, contrast, saturation, white balance, grading, colour spaces and high dynamic range.
intro: Colour decides how a video feels. These words say how it is measured, changed and kept the same from screen to screen.

title: Text and captions
description: Titles, captions and subtitles: how words appear on screen, how they are timed and how they are stored in files.
intro: Words on a video help people who cannot hear, people who watch with the sound off and people who speak another language.

title: Effects and compositing
description: Putting layers together: opacity, blend modes, masks, green screen, keyframes, blur, filters and motion graphics.
intro: Compositing means stacking pictures like sheets of glass. These words explain the stack and the tricks you do with it.

title: Formats, codecs and containers
description: What is inside a video file: containers, codecs, bitrate, resolution, frame rate, pixel formats and the standards behind them.
intro: A video file is a box (the container) that holds pictures and sound squeezed by a codec. These words tell the parts apart.

title: Delivery and platforms
description: Getting the finished video to people: exporting, aspect ratios for each app, safe areas, thumbnails, proxies and hand-off files.
intro: A video is only done when someone can watch it. These words are about exporting it and sending it where it belongs.

title: Industry slang
description: What people on a film or video team really say: B-roll, rough cut, picture lock, wrap, "fix it in post" and many more.
intro: Every job has its own way of talking. This is how video teams talk, with what each word really means.
